claims.text: As-fabricated HfNbTiVAl10 exhibits a hierarchical heterostructure containing nanoscale precipitates, multiscale grain boundaries, and spatially heterogeneous features.

Adding quantitative hierarchical microstructural descriptors to an ML regression model will improve Young’s-modulus prediction for HfNbTiVAl10 relative to conventional continuum or finite-element simulations.
Adding quantitative hierarchical microstructural descriptors to an ML regression model will improve yield-strength prediction for HfNbTiVAl10 relative to conventional simulations.
The descriptor-based ML model will improve prediction of fracture-related behavior in HfNbTiVAl10 relative to conventional simulations.
The ML model will produce predictions more rapidly than conventional continuum or finite-element simulations.
Random Forest and gradient-boosting methods can be used as regression models for HEA or refractory-alloy mechanical and elastic properties.
The proposed model will encode nanoprecipitate size, distribution, and interface characteristics extracted from microstructural data.
The proposed model will be trained using high-fidelity simulation data and experimental tensile and fracture-test data.
The scale and spatial distribution of nanoprecipitates and grain-boundary or interface characteristics mediate deformation and fracture in HfNbTiVAl10.
Multiscale microstructural descriptors allow the ML model to capture interactions governing elastic deformation, plastic deformation, and fracture.
Traditional continuum simulations contain averaging assumptions that omit relevant hierarchical microstructural detail.
Accounting for hierarchical microstructural detail will reduce prediction errors.
The ML model will predict HfNbTiVAl10 yield strength within ±15% of experimental values.
The ML model will predict HfNbTiVAl10 Young’s modulus within ±15% of experimental values.
Established simulations lacking detailed hierarchical descriptors typically deviate by more than 15% from experimental yield strength and modulus.
Established physics-based prediction methods require longer calculations than surrogate ML prediction.

Model performance may fail when descriptors cannot be extracted accurately or reproducibly, relevant phases or defects are omitted, or testing conditions differ substantially from training conditions.
Prior studies have applied ML models to yield-strength or elastic-property prediction in related HEA and refractory-alloy datasets.
Prediction gains depend on descriptor quality, dataset consistency, and adequate representation of processing-induced microstructural variation.
The hypothesis is predeclared as falsified if prediction errors exceed ±15% across a statistically significant number of independent tests.
